claim: Scientists were right to reject Wegener's continental drift.

heard.who: Henry Frankel, historian of science, University of Missouri-Kansas City, in Live Science, arguing that the lack of a mechanism was a sound reason to reject continental drift
heard.quote: "There's an irony that the key objection to continent drift was that there is no mechanism, and plate tectonics was accepted without a mechanism,"

answer: Partly. Most geologists rejected Wegener's idea, mainly because he could not explain what force could move continents, and the forces he proposed were far too weak. But the idea that continents move was later confirmed, and from the mid-1960s it became part of plate tectonics.

facts.text: Alfred Wegener proposed continental drift in 1912, and mainstream geologists rejected it at the time.

sources.title: Continental Drift: The groundbreaking theory of moving continents
sources.quote: The theory was proposed by geophysicist and meteorologist Alfred Wegener in 1912, but was rejected by mainstream science at the time.

sources.title: 4.1 Alfred Wegener's Arguments for Plate Tectonics
sources.quote: without any reasonable mechanism to make it work, Wegener's theory was quickly dismissed by most geologists of the day.

sources.title: Plate tectonics: history of an idea
sources.quote: Wegener's inability to provide an adequate explanation of the forces responsible for continental drift and the prevailing belief that the earth was solid and immovable resulted in the scientific dismissal of his theories.

facts.text: The main objection to Wegener's theory was that he could not explain what force moves continents; the forces he proposed were far too weak.

sources.title: 4.1 Alfred Wegener's Arguments for Plate Tectonics
sources.quote: The main criticism of Wegener's idea was that he could not explain how continents could move.

sources.title: Plate tectonics: history of an idea
sources.quote: generated by the rotation of the earth were calculated to be insufficient to move continents.

sources.title: When Continental Drift Was Considered Pseudoscience
sources.quote: The British ridiculed him for distorting the continents to make them fit and, more damningly, for not describing a credible mechanism powerful enough to move continents.

facts.text: The idea that continents move was later confirmed: it became part of plate tectonics, accepted from the mid-1960s, after Wegener's death.

sources.title: When Continental Drift Was Considered Pseudoscience
sources.quote: The turnabout on his theory came relatively quickly, in the mid-1960s, as older geologists died off and younger ones began to accumulate proof of seafloor spreading

sources.title: Continental Drift: The groundbreaking theory of moving continents
sources.quote: Scientists confirmed some of Wegener's ideas decades later, which are now part of the widely accepted theory of plate tectonics

sources.title: Wegener Proposes the Theory of Continental Drift
sources.quote: It wasn't until the 1960s, with advancements in the understanding of seafloor spreading and plate tectonics, that the ideas underpinning Wegener's theory gained acceptance.

contested.text: Whether the lack of a mechanism was the real reason geologists rejected drift, or whether resistance to an outsider also played a part. The USGS says leading geologists regarded him as a mere meteorologist meddling in their field.

sources.publisher: U.S. Geological Survey, This Dynamic Earth
sources.title: Alfred Lothar Wegener: Moving continents
sources.quote: Despite overwhelming criticism from most leading geologists, who regarded him as a mere meteorologist and outsider meddling in their field
